column3: The Hebrew says my hand; BSB says His hand.
The Hebrew wishes to know and find Him, without an explicit where.
The Hebrew explicitly names words and answering me; BSB says how He would answer.
The Hebrew names forward and backward; BSB specifies east and west.
The Hebrew names left and right; BSB specifies north and south.
The Hebrew calls it the way with me; BSB describes the way I have taken.
The Hebrew has my foot in the singular; BSB has feet.
The Hebrew names my prescribed portion; BSB specifies my daily bread.
The Hebrew says He is one and explicitly names His soul; BSB says unchangeable and what He desires.
The Hebrew says many such things are with Him without explicitly calling them plans.
The Hebrew has an active verb hiding darkness from my face; BSB describes thick darkness covering my face.
